clue.text: Who speaks poorly of clumsy individual following sex change?

indicators.note: a change of sex swaps the female abbreviation for the male one, so one letter is exchanged

blocks.note: someone who fumbles things is clumsy
the male abbreviation replaces the female F

explanation.surface: A question about someone who badmouths an awkward person after their transition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following sex change' tells you to turn the F (female) of FUMBLER into M (male), giving MUMBLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mumbler is a person whose speech is indistinct, i.e. one who talks badly.

clue.text: Very little to do with poetry bores mother

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A complaint that verse leaves mum cold and she has little to do with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' looks like the sense of tedium, but it means drilling in. Ode-related is the sense of the adjective used.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity, a synonym for very little.

clue.text: Film strip published cuts and charged items for incorrect subtitles?

indicators.note: something that cuts into a line splits it and sits in the gap

blocks.note: a slat is a thin strip of wood

explanation.surface: A film-strip whose published cuts and charged items lead to wrongly rendered subtitles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film strip' reads as one thing but gives two pieces, and the publishing word cuts between them. Wrong subtitles are typically bad translations, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Faulty subtitles are an example of mistranslations, renderings of dialogue into another language done wrongly.

clue.text: Comic almost upset bishop

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: A clergyman nearly loses his temper at a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: DROLL loses its last letter and is read upwards. Senior Church of England bishops sit in the House of Lords as Lords Spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is addressed as 'My Lord' and may sit among the peers, so lord is a fair title for one.

clue.text: Treasurer voided shipping item, returning proof of payment

indicators.note: something voided is emptied, so only its outside letters remain
shipping means taking on board, so a piece is carried inside
returning means going back, so the result is read in the other direction

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
a piece is an item, as in a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A treasurer cancels a shipped item and sends back the proof of payment.
explanation.walkthrough: T...R holds PIECE, and the whole of TPIECER is then reversed to give RECEIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the written acknowledgement that money has been paid.

clue.text: Duo playing with brio in private venue?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performing freely in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two musicians performing spiritedly at an exclusive gig.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a 'venue' here is a room for intimate rather than musical performances.
explanation.definitionFit: A boudoir is a lady's private bedroom or dressing room, a secluded place where things happen.

clue.text: New union members acquiring good links between banks

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the short piece is held inside the longer one

explanation.surface: Fresh trade-union recruits picking up decent connections between financial banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' and 'banks' suggest trade unions and finance; they are a marriage and riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridges are structures spanning a river and connecting one bank to the other.

clue.text: Person taking advantage of exercise regime to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone exploiting a fitness programme at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' reads as gym work but here is the verb meaning to employ.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who exploits others or a situation for their own benefit.

clue.text: Making too much of unfortunate mishap interrupting sovereign's reformation

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
to interrupt is to break into, so one set of letters goes inside the other
a reformation reshapes something, so the combined letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the possessive ending is dropped; only the word is used

explanation.surface: Overplaying an embarrassing accident that disrupted a monarch's religious reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' evokes Henry VIII's break with Rome; here it is the signal to rearrange. The possessive 's is ignored, leaving exactly fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Overemphasising is giving something more stress or importance than it deserves.

clue.text: Prize series broadcast titles regularly

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the word is heard rather than read
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a series of things in lines are rows

explanation.surface: A prize-winning TV series has its credits screened at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series broadcast' looks like a TV show; it is ROWS spoken aloud, which sounds like ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize, for instance at a show.

clue.text: Intended effect of strike affected student services

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An industrial strike achieving its aim by disrupting campus services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a military strike, which aims to cause damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Destructiveness is the capacity to wreck, which is what a military strike is meant to have.

clue.text: Constable's foremost painting, perhaps The Hay Wain?

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so just the first letter is kept

blocks.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Asking whether Constable's best-known picture is The Hay Wain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hay Wain is John Constable's famous painting; read literally, the title names a hay wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A wain is an old word for a farm wagon, so a hay wain is an example of a cart.

clue.text: Clear information reduced area of high pressure

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: clear skies, reduced data, and a high-pressure area.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In meteorology a ridge is an elongated region of high atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Speculate over end of model's career

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the following word
over here means covering on both sides, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to bet is to gamble or speculate

explanation.surface: Guessing about how a fashion model's working life will finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun for a job but is the verb to rush headlong, as BELT is.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt along and to career both mean to move at great speed.

clue.text: Ask personal questions about four ladies?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to pry is to be nosy

explanation.surface: Being nosy about a group of four women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' in Britain also means a women's public toilet, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A privy is an old word for a toilet, and the ladies is a lavatory for women.

clue.text: Lay to rest popular theory presented regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so alternate letters are kept

explanation.surface: Burying a popular theory that keeps being trotted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay to rest' suggests dismissing an idea, but it is the literal burial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, a literal laying to rest.

clue.text: Live in unused part of religious building

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to be or live, as in 'we are'

explanation.surface: Taking up residence in a disused corner of a church or temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unused' reads as neglected, but it is MINT as in brand-new.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Inaccurate essay overlooking article covering sleep's part in nervous system

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so something is left out
inaccurate means not correct, so the letters are wrongly ordered
covering means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A sloppy essay on sleep's role in the nervous system.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of ESSAY, rearrange the rest, and wrap it around NAP; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synapse is the junction between two nerve cells across which signals pass.

clue.text: Country initially bombed by a de Havilland

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: Olivia de Havilland was a Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: A country bombed by a de Havilland aircraft, such as a Mosquito.
explanation.walkthrough: De Havilland suggests the British aircraft maker; it is the actress Olivia de Havilland of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked South American nation.

clue.text: Where one might hear roars of support introducing Prime Minister cut short

indicators.note: cut short means trimmed at the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: to bear is to carry or support
William Pitt (Elder or Younger) was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Cheers of support as a Prime Minister is interrupted in a rowdy chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: PITT loses its last letter. 'Roars of support' suggests a crowd, but the def is a place where bears roar; the Commons is also called a bear pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear pit was a sunken enclosure for keeping or baiting bears, which roar.

clue.text: They may show the world to half-hearted young women

indicators.note: half-hearted means half the heart is missing, so one of the two middle letters goes

blocks.note: at and to both mark direction, as in throw at or throw to

explanation.surface: Offering to show the world to some unenthusiastic girls.
explanation.walkthrough: LASSES has a double S at its centre; losing half of that heart leaves LASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlases are books of maps, which may depict the whole world.

clue.text: Before and after usual time? Maybe prior

blocks.note: late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: Asking about being early and late, with 'prior' seeming to mean 'beforehand'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like another word for before, but it is the religious superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior heads a priory, and such senior churchmen are classed as prelates.

clue.text: Selectively do away with best out of operation

blocks.note: the pick of the bunch is the best
a machine that is off is not operating

explanation.surface: Removing the top people from a project one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best out of' looks like a phrase, but the words split as best + out of operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick off is to kill or eliminate targets one by one, as a sniper does.

clue.text: He or I (not him or me)?

definitions.text: He or I (not him or me)?

blocks.note: surface reading: the subject pronouns of grammar
setter's reading: the bracket rules out pronouns, so He and I are chemical symbols, helium and iodine

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a grammar note about object pronouns; it actually tells you He and I are not pronouns at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and iodine are chemical substances that cannot be broken down further, each listed in the periodic table.

clue.text: Opposed to transatlantic checks and insubstantial borders

indicators.note: checks here means holds back or contains, so the letters sit inside the word
borders here means surrounds on each side, so the answer lies within the word

blocks.note: a second word containing the same four letters, confirming the first hiding place

explanation.surface: Against transatlantic inspections and borders that are weak.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue doubles up: transatlantic checks the answer, and insubstantial borders it as well, since both words hold the same four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning against, opposed to.

clue.text: Notice that displays information about The Times

definitions.text: that displays information about The Times

blocks.note: first meaning: to spot, in slang

blocks.clueFragment: that displays information about The Times
blocks.note: second meaning: a device showing the time of day

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is just the times of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock as a verb is British slang for noticing; as a noun it is the instrument that tells the hour.

clue.text: Learned one's coming between partners holding hands

indicators.note: coming between means going into the middle, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: West and East are partners at bridge, each holding a hand of cards
one is I, and 's is is

explanation.surface: A learned person squeezing between a couple holding hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding hands' sounds romantic, but the partners are bridge players holding hands of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) means erudite, and a wise person is knowledgeable.

clue.text: Marine life's apex predator

indicators.note: apex is the top, and in a down clue the top letter is the first

explanation.surface: A natural-history description of the top hunter in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while SEA plus the top of 'life' builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals are carnivorous marine mammals that hunt fish, and the leopard seal is a top predator.

clue.text: Come to terms with female being able to do things well

blocks.clueFragment: being able to do things well

explanation.surface: A capable woman learning to accept something.
explanation.walkthrough: ACE is the adjective meaning excellent at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a problem is to confront and accept it, much as coming to terms with it.

clue.text: Make more businesslike declaration with reporter's associates

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so the following word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a profession of faith is a declaration

explanation.surface: A firm smartens up by issuing a statement through a journalist's contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declaration' hides PROFESSION in its sense of an avowal, as in a profession of love.
explanation.definitionFit: To professionalise something is to give it the standards of a profession, making it more business-like.

clue.text: Support the French suppressing Republican struggles

indicators.note: to suppress is to keep out of sight, so a letter disappears

blocks.note: a truss is a supporting frame or bandage

explanation.surface: French backing for crushing a Republican uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suppressing' looks like the French holding the Republican down, but it means the R is removed from the support word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussles are scuffles or vigorous struggles.

clue.text: Dispute to do with charges for transportation

indicators.note: with here means accompanied by inside, so one piece is held in the other

explanation.surface: An argument concerning shipping fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freight' usually means the cargo itself, but it can also mean the fee charged for carrying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight can mean the payment made for transporting goods, so it covers transport charges.
